newsitem.title: USA: Ohio expects $864 mln fiscal 1997 fund balance.
newsitem.headline: Ohio expects $864 mln fiscal 1997 fund balance.

text.p: Ohio Budget Director Greg Browning told lawmakers this week the state expects to close fiscal 1997 with an $864.2 million fund balance, nearly $400 million more than anticipated for budget recommendations earlier this year.

Browning attributed the increase to a better-than-expected economy and told lawmakers on the budget conference committee Monday that the majority of the revenues should address Ohio public school funding needs.

The executive budget submitted to the General Assembly in January included a projected fund balance of $472.2 million. The Legislative Budget Office originally projected a $646 million fund balance and upped its own estimate in April to $766.9 million.

Browning told lawmakers it would be prudent to use a portion of the fund balance to make a down payment on the Ohio Supreme Court's school funding decision from March and cap tax relief proposals at $285.7 million.
A school building assistance bond program could receive $132.2 million of the fund balance in addition to the $125 million already set aside by the Senate, Browning said.

Browning also said Ohio tax revenue projections for fiscal 1997 have been revised up by $218 million from the original executive budget estimates based on higher estimated receipts from personal income taxes.
Tax receipt projections has been raised $188.7 million for fiscal 1998 and by $146.2 million for fiscal 1999, Browning added.
Browning also said the administration of Gov. George Voinovich supports the creation of a budget stabilization fund for schools, often referred to as a "rainy day" fund.
